title: No fine for driving alone: traffic police call congestion fine fake

slides.head: No fine for driving alone: traffic police call congestion fine fake
What happened
slides.body: On Nov 26 the traffic police posted a fake news alert: there is no fine for travelling alone in a car, and claims of a new 'congestion fine' are unverified.

slides.head: Why it matters
slides.body: The reels followed Cyberabad Moves 2026, where mobility experts from Bogotá and London suggested congestion charges and parking reforms in a panel discussion.

slides.head: Fine for driving alone
slides.body: A Cyberabad Moves survey counted 10,138 people driving alone near Cyber Towers in one morning peak.

slides.head: Dig deeper
slides.body: 10,138 people drove alone near Cyber Towers in the morning peak; 3,584 travelled two to a car.

slides.head: What to watch
slides.body: Whether any parking or congestion policy is formally proposed; police say none is on the table now. Ask: If a congestion charge were ever proposed, who would decide it and how would the public be consulted?

slides.head: Spill the tea, daily
slides.body: Hyderabad news in 30 seconds, with the numbers and the questions. Follow for tomorrow's drop: spillthetea.news

No fine for driving alone: traffic police call congestion fine fake

Hyderabad Traffic Police flagged social media posts and reels claiming motorists would be fined for travelling alone in a car as false; no congestion penalty has been proposed.

Why it matters: The reels followed Cyberabad Moves 2026, where mobility experts from Bogotá and London suggested congestion charges and parking reforms in a panel discussion.

Source: The Hindu. Image: The Hindu
